scenarios.name: Escalation in Middle East Oil Disruption
scenarios.description: Tensions between Israel and Iran escalate into direct military confrontation, disrupting oil shipping in the Persian Gulf. This causes crude oil prices to spike by $30-50 per barrel, increasing import costs and stagflationary pressures.

impacts.explanation: Higher energy prices directly increase CPI components including transportation and housing costs.
Sticky inflation forces Fed to hike rates despite weak growth signals.
Energy cost shocks reduce industrial output margins and production efficiency.
Higher import prices worsen the trade deficit even if volume stays constant.

scenarios.reasoning: Current intelligence indicates elevated military readiness in the region. Base rate historically shows 20-25% probability of major escalation during periods of high regional tension. Recent drone incidents near Saudi facilities suggest proximity to threshold.

scenarios.name: US-China Trade Deal Breakthrough
scenarios.description: After months of negotiation deadlock, the US and China agree to a phased tariff reduction framework focusing on technology transfer and agricultural purchases. Markets rally on improved supply chain certainty.

impacts.explanation: Improved consumer confidence and business investment boost retail spending.
Increased Chinese soybean and consumer goods imports narrow the gap partially.
Export demand recovery adds to growth through net exports component.
Risk-on sentiment increases yield demand as growth outlook improves.

scenarios.reasoning: Both nations face domestic economic headwinds making compromise more attractive. Historical precedent from 2018-2020 trade negotiations shows about 30-40% likelihood of breakthrough when negotiations extend beyond typical cycle. Recent conciliatory language from both sides supports this estimate.

scenarios.name: Aggressive Federal Reserve Rate Cuts
scenarios.description: The August CPI report shows core inflation dropping below 2%, pushing the Fed to cut rates aggressively by 100 basis points to stimulate an economy showing signs of weakening labor markets.

impacts.explanation: Direct policy action lowers the federal funds target rate.
Rate cuts compress long-end yields through Expectations theory channel.
Lower mortgage rates make housing more affordable, spurring construction rebound.
Weaker demand and base effects pull headline inflation lower.

scenarios.reasoning: Current inflation trajectory appears to be moderating. Based on historical Fed behavior since 1990, once core CPI sustainably breaks 2% there is approximately 70% chance of rate cuts within two quarters. Given current data trajectory aligns with early stages of that pattern.

scenarios.name: Eurozone Debt Crisis Resurgence
scenarios.description: Italy's sovereign debt faces renewed pressure after populist government policies trigger credit rating downgrade. Contagion spreads to Spain and Portugal, causing financial market turbulence and global risk repricing.

impacts.explanation: Flight-to-quality bidding drives yields lower despite no fundamental US change.
Stronger USD from safe-haven flows hurts US export competitiveness.
Financial tightening impacts investment spending component.
Wealth effects and credit availability constraints reduce consumer spending.

scenarios.reasoning: European political fragmentation remains elevated. From Tetlock’s reference class of post-2010 EMU crises, about 20% recur episodically every few years due to unresolved fiscal architecture flaws. Current Italian deficit projections exceed EU limits triggering similar dynamics.

scenarios.name: Tech Sector Regulatory Crackdown
scenarios.description: Congress passes comprehensive antitrust legislation targeting large tech platforms, forcing divestitures and data sharing requirements. Stock valuations drop sharply affecting wealth effects and corporate investment plans.

impacts.explanation: Reduced business fixed investment in software and equipment drags on growth.
Layoffs in affected sectors increase measured unemployment temporarily.
Wealth destruction reduces discretionary consumer spending particularly online retail.
Datacenter and device manufacturing contraction lowers industrial output.

scenarios.reasoning: Bipartisan momentum exists around tech regulation. Applying Tetlock’s scoring system, past regulatory waves had ~25% passage probability when introduced but failed within 6 months. However current political climate appears more receptive than previous cycles suggesting elevated odds.

scenarios.name: Climate Policy Shock - Green New Deal Implementation
scenarios.description: Congressional budget reconciliation passes sweeping climate legislation with massive infrastructure spending and carbon pricing mechanism, reorienting capital allocation toward clean energy at expense of traditional industries.

impacts.explanation: Large infrastructure spending injection boosts near-term GDP via fiscal multiplier effect.
Fiscal expansion combined with energy transition bottlenecks push prices higher.
Massive new spending significantly increases federal debt issuance requirements.
Clean energy construction boom drives industrial equipment production surge.

scenarios.reasoning: While climate action enjoys broad support, full Green New Deal implementation requires extensive legislative coordination unlikely absent supermajority. Historical analysis of major structural reforms suggests only 10-15% probability of full passage within standard timeframe given current partisan divide.

scenarios.name: Global Recession Triggered by China Slowdown
scenarios.description: China's real estate crisis deepens triggering broader economic contraction. Export demand collapse affects German autos, Japanese electronics, and US multinationals leading to synchronized global slowdown.

impacts.explanation: Collapse in export orders and multinational profits reduce US economic activity.
Manufacturing and export sectors lay off workers due to demand collapse.
Collapse in import volumes due to weak domestic demand improves measured balance.
Reduced export manufacturing sharply contracts industrial output.

scenarios.reasoning: China property sector stress well documented. Among advanced economies, external shock transmission historically occurs with roughly 10-15% probability during periods of significant Chinese slowdown based on 2008 and 2015 episodes. Current indicators suggest moderate rather than severe downturn.
